title: Kelvedon Spice Named Essex Restaurant of the Year at ARTA 2026
excerpt: The Kelvedon High Street restaurant serving Indian and Bangladeshi dishes beat a field of more than 1,250 nominees to take the county title at the London Hilton ceremony on October 12.
body:
• Kelvedon Spice, on Kelvedon High Street near Colchester, has been named Essex Restaurant of the Year at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards 2026.
  • The title was announced on October 12 at the London Hilton on Park Lane, from a field of more than 1,250 nominated businesses across the UK.
  • The restaurant serves traditional Indian and Bangladeshi dishes, tandoori specialities and biryanis, with chef's dishes including Roushon Chilli and Naga Chicken.
  • It is the latest honour for owner and chef Imran Ahmed, whose restaurant also won the Essex regional title at ARTA 2025 and a Best Restaurant prize at the 2024 Curry Life Awards.

Kelvedon Spice, a restaurant on the high street of the Essex village of Kelvedon, has been named the best restaurant in the county at a national awards ceremony celebrating Britain's Asian restaurant and takeaway sector.

The restaurant won Essex Restaurant of the Year at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards 2026, according to the Colchester Gazette. The winners were announced on October 12 at the London Hilton on Park Lane, at a ceremony hosted by TV news anchor Samantha Simmonds and comedian Paul Sinha.

A repeat winner, not a one-off

This is not the first time Kelvedon Spice has left an awards night with a trophy. The restaurant, run by owner and chef Imran Ahmed, won the Best Restaurant category at the 2024 Curry Life Awards, when Ahmed said he was thrilled by the recognition. It then took the regional restaurant title for Essex at ARTA 2025, before returning this year to win the county honour again in the 2026 edition.

That sequence matters. One award can be a good night. Three in three years, from two different awards bodies, points to a kitchen that has held its standard while the sector around it has been squeezed by rising employment costs, food prices and energy bills — pressures the awards' organisers themselves put at the centre of this year's ceremony.

What is on the menu

Kelvedon Spice serves traditional Indian and Bangladeshi dishes, the twin roots of most British curry-house cooking, where Bangladeshi chefs built the high-street restaurant trade over decades. Alongside the classics, the menu lists tandoori specialities and biryanis, plus a set of chef's dishes that carry the kitchen's signature.

Two of those dishes name their heat honestly. Roushon Chilli and Naga Chicken both draw on the naga chilli, one of the hottest chillies used in Bangladeshi cooking in Britain and a flavour strongly associated with the Sylheti tradition that underpins much of the UK's curry industry. For diners, the offer is a familiar format — tandoori, biryani, house specials — executed to a level that has now been judged the best in Essex twice running.

A strong night for Essex

Kelvedon Spice was not the county's only winner. Kusturi Indian Restaurant in Colchester took both Essex Chef of the Year and National Chef of the Year, while Kaani Kaana in Upminster won Essex Takeaway of the Year and National Takeaway of the Year. Other Essex finalists this year included Moonlight Tandoori in Harlow, Crown of India in Loughton and Pink Chilliz on Canvey, alongside shortlisted restaurants in Chelmsford, Coggeshall, Benfleet and Ongar.

ARTA says its judging starts with public nominations covering food quality, service and value for money, followed by checks of Google and Tripadvisor reviews and food hygiene ratings. More than 1,250 businesses were nominated for the 2026 awards.

"This industry represents far more than food. It is an integral part of multicultural Britain."

— Mohammed Munim, founder and chief executive, ARTA

What it means

For the diaspora, results like these are a reminder of where Britain's Indian food culture actually lives: not only in big-city dining rooms, but in village high streets, where family-run restaurants serve mixed local audiences night after night. Kelvedon is a small village between Colchester and Chelmsford, and its restaurant now holds a county title decided on a London stage.

ARTA founder and chief executive Mohammed Munim used the ceremony to argue that independent restaurants are still investing in quality, their teams and the customer experience despite the cost pressures on hospitality. Kelvedon Spice's run of awards — Curry Life in 2024, ARTA in 2025 and again in 2026 — is a concrete example of that claim. The test now is the ordinary one every award winner faces: turning a trophy into bookings, and bookings into another year at the same standard.
